overview: Schistosomiasis is an acute and chronic parasitic disease caused by blood flukes (trematode worms) of the genus Schistosoma. Estimates show that at least 253.7 million people required preventive treatment in 2024. Preventive treatment, which should be repeated over a number of years, will reduce and prevent morbidity.
symptoms: accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal cavity
hypertension of the abdominal blood vessels
fibrosis of the bladder and ureter
nodules in the vulva (female genital schistosomiasis)
pathology of the seminal vesicles, prostate and other organs
transmission: larval forms of the parasite released by freshwater snails
risk_factors: lack of access to safe drinking water and adequate sanitation
women doing domestic chores in infested water
complications: ectopic pregnancies due to female genital schistosomiasis
key_facts: Schistosomiasis transmission has been reported from 79 countries.
At least 93.9% of those requiring treatment for schistosomiasis live in Africa.
Deaths due to schistosomiasis are estimated at 14,353 globally per year.
